body:
> **Status (2026-10-02, round 5).** Round 5 is pushed at `9d6351b0`. It fixes the red CI at `ef19980f` (env registration: `FLY_MACHINE_ID` and the `SFEE_SETTLEMENT_SWEEP_ENABLED` default), merges main `b9ee8e0a` (#604, #629) with a merge commit, and implements the owner's decision **OR-111-1**: TGP keeps its 2% on refunds and chargebacks, the coach gets an alert with exact amounts, the coach's share comes back from that sale's own transfer, and what is still owed is held from the coach's next sale(s) by forward netting. Round 4's 90-day clawback of the coach's other transfers is removed. The round-4 activation hold is replaced by the owner's decision (residual accepted). Needs an independent audit. Do not merge.

## Tier header

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **Tier** | **T4** |
| **Why** | Changes how real money moves for every coach-package sale: Stripe charge mechanism (destination charge + application fee → separate charges and transfers with `on_behalf_of`), transfer amounts, refund/dispute recovery, a new money ledger (migration with RLS), and the reported coach net. |
| **T4 trigger scan** | Payments/Stripe money movement: YES. New tables + RLS policies (`ChargeSettlement`, `PayeeRecovery`, `CronLease`): YES. New scheduled job that moves money (15-minute payout / settlement sweep): YES. New env kill switch `SFEE_SETTLEMENT_SWEEP_ENABLED` (registered in `ENV_RULES`, `prod-switches.yml`, `.env.example`): YES. Unique-index swap on `SplitLedgerEntry`: YES. Round 3: per-charge money lock (one `CronLease` row per charge while money moves) and a nullable `CronLease.cursor` column, both inside the same unmerged migration `20270210000000`: YES. Round 4: new table `TransferReversalOp` (RLS enabled + forced, service-role and owner policies), `ConnectTransfer.reversal_seq` / `recovery_clawback_cents`, `ChargeSettlement.reconcile_requested_at` / `reconcile_dispute_id` / `reconcile_reason` + index, all inside `20270210000000`; the sweep gains money-moving steps (re-drive pending reversals, re-run flagged adjustments): YES. Round 5 (OR-111-1): money semantics change (TGP keeps its full 2% on refunded and charged-back sales; the coach bears it), new table `PayoutAdjustmentNotice` inside `20270210000000` (CHECKs, FK cascade, RLS enabled + forced, service-role / owner / payee-select policies), removal of round 4's `ConnectTransfer.recovery_clawback_cents` and `TransferReversalOp.recovery_id` (never merged) and of the 90-day clawback step, new coach-facing push + email on refunds and chargebacks, new env rule `FLY_MACHINE_ID` (read-only Fly runtime value, no new secret): YES. CI gate files: `prisma/schema-parity-baseline.sql` YES, one line deleted only (the `SplitLedgerEntry_purchase_kind_payee_idx` rename item, because this migration drops that index; the gate requires deleting fixed items). No workflow, `scripts/ci/*` or branch-protection change. Auth/tenancy: no auth change; new RLS mirrors `SplitLedgerEntry`/`ConnectTransfer`. |
| **T3 trigger scan** | Public API response shape: additive only (`recoveries_cents`, `net_cents` on the earnings summary and `getCoachEarnings`); `/coach/connect/metrics` `net_30d` now uses the shared net (it double-subtracted refunds before). Round 5 adds two coach routes: `GET /v1/coach/payments/adjustments` (held balance + notices, caller-scoped) and `POST /v1/coach/payments/adjustments/:id/acknowledge`. New email template `coach-payout-adjustment`. No mobile change in this PR (the Money page reads the new route when it is built). |
| **Bounded T1** | None. Every hunk is part of the T4 change. |
| **Builder-owner** | Builder lane B-FEE (S-FEE). Owner priority #1. |
| **Acceptance evidence** | Worked examples, invariant sweep (5000 charges), refund / dispute / renewal / head-coach / free / legacy scenarios and reconciliation identity in `test/s-fee-charge-settlement.spec.ts`; scheduled sweep (lease race with two runners, kill switch, bounds, failure codes, overlapping sweeps pay once) in `test/s-fee-settlement-sweep.spec.ts`; round 3: concurrent / duplicate refunds and disputes (the Opus probe as assertions) in `test/s-fee-charge-concurrency.spec.ts`, missed-renewal backfill by charge id in `test/s-fee-renewal-backfill.spec.ts`; round 4: fencing, keyed reversals, canonical disputes and cash-vs-receivable in `test/s-fee-r4-money-protocol.spec.ts`; round 5: the three OR-111-1 worked examples, notices, Money API, delivery and the netting race in `test/s-fee-r5-or-111-1.spec.ts` (10 of 11 fail on the round-4 code; the money-formatting test is a control); updated suites listed under Tests. CI at head. |
| **Promotion triggers** | Already T4 (highest). Round 2 added a money-moving scheduled job, a new table and an env kill switch; round 3 adds the per-charge lock and the cursor column; round 4 adds the reversal-operation table and money-moving sweep steps; round 5 changes refund/dispute economics and adds the notice table and coach alerts. Tier stays T4. |

## Owner decision OR-111-1 (2026-10-02)

Owner, verbatim: "A coach sells a package -> customer chargebacks -> we send the coach an alert, we sent the customer $xxx,, that wer'e holding the sum of our 2% fee and the stripe fees from his next sale, in addition to the standard charges - make sense? Basically we will settle up by wage gouging!"

OR-111-1, as recorded by the operator:
1. On a refund or a chargeback, the coach gets an alert (push + Money "needs attention" + email when the provider is live) with exact amounts: what the customer got back, and the amount TGP is holding from the coach's next sale = TGP's 2% + every Stripe fee on that charge (processing fee Stripe keeps, dispute fee), on top of the next sale's standard fees.
2. The coach's share of the refunded charge comes back by reversing that charge's own transfer; whatever Stripe refuses (coach already paid out) joins the held amount.
3. Recovery is forward-only netting: the held amount is deducted from the coach's next transfer(s) until fully settled (carried across sales; Money page shows the open balance). No payout delay, no `debit_negative_balances`, no Account Debits, no reversal of the coach's other past sales' transfers (supersedes round 4's 90-day clawback).
4. Won disputes / reinstatements net against the open balance. A coach who never sells again leaves an open receivable: `SFEE_RECOVERY_OPEN` alert to the operator/owner (accepted residual; production has 0 paid sales).

## Problem

Checkout created Stripe destination charges with `application_fee_amount` (2%, plus 5% head-coach split). With destination charges Stripe takes its processing fee from the platform: "Your platform pays the Stripe fee after the `application_fee_amount` is transferred to your account." ([Stripe: destination charges](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/destination-charges.md?platform=web&integration=custom&ui=elements&api-integration=paymentintents)). So the coach received price - 2% and TGP paid about 2.9% + 30c out of its 2%, losing roughly 0.9% + 30c per US card sale, and more on international cards, refunds and disputes. Owner ruling (09-30): coach payout = price - card processing - TGP 2%, client pays the listed price, no surcharge.

## Mechanism chosen: separate charges and transfers, with `on_behalf_of`

1. Every paid checkout path (Checkout Session, PaymentSheet PaymentIntent, guest one-time PaymentIntent, guest and member subscriptions) now charges on the platform with `on_behalf_of` = the coach's connected account and **no** `transfer_data`, `application_fee_amount` or `application_fee_percent`.
2. When a charge succeeds (`checkout.session.completed`, `payment_intent.succeeded`, `invoice.paid` for the first invoice and every renewal, guest conversion, or the backstop sweeper), `ChargeSettlementService` reads the charge with `balance_transaction` expanded. `balance_transaction.fee` is Stripe's actual fee, including international-card and currency-conversion pricing.
3. `computeChargeSplit` in `src/payouts-v2/platform-fee.service.ts` is the single fee function (checkout, FeePolicyService plan, payouts-v2 `compute()` all call it):
   - platform fee = floor(gross x 200 bps), head-coach split = floor(gross x 500 bps) when the seller is a sub-coach with a paid-out head coach
   - coach net = gross - actual Stripe fee - platform fee - head-coach split (rounding goes to the coach; TGP never takes more than its bps)
4. Transfers are created with `source_transaction` = the charge and idempotency keys `tgp-settle-<charge>-coach|head_coach`, so each renewal is paid from its own charge exactly once. TGP keeps exactly its fee, so platform net = platform fee >= 0 for every charge.

Stripe evidence:
- "When using separate charges and transfers, the platform can collect fees on a charge by reducing the amount it transfers to the destination accounts." and the platform "account balance is debited for the cost of the Stripe fees, refunds, and chargebacks." ([Stripe: separate charges and transfers](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/separate-charges-and-transfers.md?platform=web&integration=checkout&ui=stripe-hosted)). Because we transfer after reading the real fee, the fee lands on the coach's side of the split, not on TGP.
- `source_transaction`: the transfer request succeeds, but "we don't execute the transfer until the funds from that charge are available in the platform account", and "The amount of the transfer must not exceed the amount of the source charge." (same page). Coach net is always below the charge amount.
- Subscriptions: "For separate charges and transfers, create the subscription on the platform with `on_behalf_of`" and create transfers separately per paid invoice ([Stripe: Connect subscriptions](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/subscriptions)).
- Refunds: "refunding a charge has no impact on any associated transfers. It's up to your platform to reconcile any amount owed back to it by reducing subsequent transfer amounts or by reversing transfers." ([Stripe: SCT with PaymentIntents](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/separate-charges-and-transfers.md?platform=web&integration=custom&ui=elements&api-integration=paymentintents)). Stripe's "processing fees from the original transaction aren't returned" ([Stripe: refunds](https://docs.stripe.com/refunds)).
- Disputes: "For destination charges and separate charges and transfers, with or without `on_behalf_of`, Stripe debits dispute amounts and fees from your platform account." Stripe recommends listening for `charge.dispute.created` and recovering funds "by reversing the transfer", and "If you challenge the dispute and win, you can transfer the funds that you previously reversed back to the connected account." ([Stripe: Connect disputes](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/disputes)).

Trade-offs considered:
- **Keep destination charges and raise the application fee by an estimated Stripe fee** (what guest one-time checkout did): the fee is only known after the charge, so estimates are wrong for international cards, currency conversion, wallets and pricing changes; TGP can still go negative. Rejected.
- **Destination charges + Account Debits** to pull the fee back from the coach: requires the platform to be responsible for negative balances and "legally binding consent" from each connected account ([Stripe: account debits](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/account-debits)). Owner/legal decision; not chosen. It remains the way to close the residual risk below.
- **Separate charges and transfers (chosen)**: exact actual-fee split per charge, one code path for one-time, guest and renewals, Stripe-recommended refund/dispute recovery. Costs: the platform holds funds until transfer (seconds after the charge is available), transfers are our code (idempotent, swept), and a refund after the coach has been paid out needs a recovery (below).

## Refunds and disputes (OR-111-1)

Voluntary cancel is unchanged: access continues through the paid period, no refund, no transfer movement. When a refund or dispute does happen, `computeAdjustedTargets` re-derives every party's target for that charge and the settlement converges each payee to it:
- `platform_fee' = platform_fee`: TGP keeps its 2% of the sale on every refund and dispute (round 4 pro-rated it down to 0). Head-coach split stays pro-rated by what the client kept.
- Coach target = what the client kept - Stripe's processing fee (not returned on refunds) - dispute fee - TGP 2% - head-coach split. A negative target is what the coach owes on that charge.
- Mechanics: reverse **that charge's own** coach transfer (round 4's durable `TransferReversalOp` with keyed, fenced, uncertainty-safe reversals is unchanged). Whatever the reversal cannot recover (TGP's 2%, the processing fee, the dispute fee, or a reversal Stripe refuses because the coach was already paid out) is a `PayeeRecovery` ("held"). It is netted from the coach's next transfer(s), carried across sales until settled. Nothing else is reversed: round 4's clawback of the coach's other transfers is removed.
- Won disputes and reinstatements first release the hold on that charge, then net any other open balance, then reinstate the rest by transfer.
- Every change in what the coach holds or got back records one `PayoutAdjustmentNotice` row (idempotent on charge + leg + event + state) under the charge lock, in the same convergence. Delivery is separate and claim-once: in-app (Money "needs attention") + push via `NotificationsService` (`COACH_ALERT` kind, so the coach's preferences apply) and email template `coach-payout-adjustment` (log transport until the provider is live; idempotency key = notice key). The webhook delivers right away; the 15-minute sweep re-delivers any notice that failed (up to 6 attempts). For settlement charges the old generic "Refund processed" coach alert is replaced by this notice, so the coach gets one alert with the real numbers.
- Legacy destination charges (renewals of subscriptions created before this PR) are detected from the charge itself (`transfer`, `transfer_data`, `application_fee`) and keep the old reversal path unchanged.

Coach copy (plain words, no exclamation marks, body at most 160 characters), for example: "A client got $100.00 back. We took $94.80 back from that sale's payout. We will hold $5.20 from your next sale." The Money API (`GET /v1/coach/payments/adjustments`) returns the open held balance per currency and each notice with its breakdown lines: TGP fee (2% of the sale), Stripe processing fee, dispute fee, and "share we could not take back from that sale's payout".

## Never settled

Purchases with `amount_cents <= 0` (free packages, invite-code grants from #595) and $0 charges (100% coupons) never create a settlement row, ledger slice, transfer, recovery or revenue. Guarded in `onChargeSucceeded`, `settleCharge`, `settlePurchase` and `applyAdjustments`; tested.

## Ledger (per charge)

`ChargeSettlement` (one row per Stripe charge, unique on charge id): gross, stripe_fee, platform_fee, head_coach_split, coach_net, refunded, dispute withdrawn/fee, current targets, rail, bps, currency. DB CHECK: when settled, stripe_fee + platform_fee + head_coach_split + coach_net = gross; platform fee and its target are never negative. `SplitLedgerEntry` gets four slices per charge (`application_fee`, `stripe_fee`, `destination`, `head_coach_split`), unique on (purchase, kind, payee, charge) as `SplitLedgerEntry_purchase_kind_payee_charge_key` (explicit map: Prisma's default name would exceed 63 chars). The migration drops the old 3-column unique under both names it can have (`SplitLedgerEntry_purchase_kind_payee_idx` from the chain, `..._purchase_id_kind_payee_user_id_key` from Prisma naming). `ConnectTransfer` gains `settlement_id`, `kind`, `netted_recovery_cents`.

## Reported net (same number everywhere)

`coachNetCents(posted, recoveries)` in `src/connect/fees/coach-net.ts` is the one definition. `GET /v1/coach/payments/earnings` summary adds `recoveries_cents` and `net_cents`; `AdminAnalyticsService.getCoachEarnings` adds them per seller / head-coach role; `/coach/connect/metrics` `net_30d` = `as_seller.net_cents`. Before, `net_30d` subtracted refunds from a posted figure that reversals had already reduced.

## Scheduled payout / settlement sweep (round 2)

`src/checkout/settlement-sweep.cron.ts` runs `@Cron('*/15 * * * *')` and calls the same `runTransferSweeper` as `POST /v1/admin/payments/transfers/run-sweeper`. That first retries settlements still waiting for Stripe's fee and settles recent paid purchases no webhook settled, then posts due transfers.
- **Single runner across Fly machines:** a `CronLease` row (`sfee-settlement-sweep`, 10-minute lease) is taken in one conditional UPDATE (`lease_until < now`), or one INSERT on the primary key. A machine that loses the race skips the tick (`SFEE_SWEEP_SKIPPED_LOCK_HELD`). The lease expires on its own, so a crashed machine blocks at most one lease; it is released when the run ends. No advisory locks (unsafe behind the pooler).
- **Idempotent per charge and transfer:** `ChargeSettlement` is unique per charge. `ConnectTransfer.idempotency_key` is unique and is the Stripe Idempotency-Key (`tgp-settle-<charge>-<leg>`). Even two overlapping sweeps (lease expired mid-run) pay each coach once; this is tested.
- **Bounded:** 25 settlements plus 50 transfers per run, and no new work starts after 8 minutes (inside the lease; `SFEE_SWEEP_DEADLINE_REACHED`).
- **Retries with backoff:** each transfer row keeps its own backoff (1, 5, 15, 60, 240, 1440 minutes, max 6 attempts) and then becomes `failed`.
- **Kill switch:** `SFEE_SETTLEMENT_SWEEP_ENABLED=false` pauses scheduled runs (`SFEE_SWEEP_DISABLED`); the admin endpoint still works. Defaults to on. Registered in `ENV_RULES`, `prod-switches.yml` and `.env.example`.
- **Log / alert codes:**
  - Transfer: `SFEE_TRANSFER_FAILED`, `SFEE_TRANSFER_PLATFORM_BALANCE_INSUFFICIENT`, `SFEE_TRANSFER_ACCOUNT_RESTRICTED`, each with a `_FINAL` suffix when retries are exhausted. These are also stored as the `last_error` prefix.
  - Sweep: `SFEE_SWEEP_FAILED`, `SFEE_SWEEP_LOCK_ERROR`, `SFEE_SWEEP_TRANSFERS_FAILED`, `SFEE_SWEEP_DEADLINE_REACHED`, `SFEE_SWEEP_DONE`.
  - Settlement: `SFEE_SETTLEMENT_RETRY_FAILED`, `SFEE_SETTLEMENT_FAILED`.
  - Lines that need a person (platform balance, restricted account, final failures, sweep failure, lease error) are error level and carry `alert=true`.

### Round 3: missed renewals and stale money (B-627-1)

- **Renewals matched by charge id.** Each run walks Stripe's paid invoices from the last 35 days (`GET /v1/invoices?status=paid&created[gte]=...`, 100 per page, 4 pages per run, newest first). It settles every invoice charge that has no `ChargeSettlement` row, matched by **charge id**. A purchase that already has a settlement is no longer skipped, so a renewal whose `invoice.paid` webhook was lost still gets paid. The run stops at its `limit` / deadline. Its position is saved in `CronLease.cursor` (`sfee-invoice-backfill-cursor`), so the next run carries on from there, and the cursor resets once it reaches the end of the window. Only S-FEE purchases are backfilled: those with an S-FEE settlement, or with no settlement and no legacy ledger rows. Legacy destination subscriptions stay on their own flow. Log codes: `SFEE_INVOICE_BACKFILL`, `SFEE_INVOICE_BACKFILL_FAILED`.
- **We never lose a charge we were told about.** If the first `retrieveCharge` fails, an `awaiting_fee` row is still written (`last_error` `SFEE_SETTLEMENT_STRIPE_UNAVAILABLE`), and the sweeper retries it. A provisional row for a charge that turns out to be $0 is deleted.
- **Purchase-level orphan window** goes from 14 to 35 days.
- **Stale alerts** (error level, `alert=true`): `SFEE_SETTLEMENT_STALE` fires when `awaiting_fee` rows are older than 1 h, and `SFEE_TRANSFER_STALE` when settlement transfers have been pending for more than 1 h. The sweep summary returns `invoices_scanned`, `invoices_backfilled`, `stale_awaiting` and `stale_transfers`.

## Concurrency: one money movement per charge at a time (round 3, B-627-2)

- **Per-charge lock.** `ChargeLock` (`src/connect/fees/charge-lock.ts`) holds one `CronLease` row per charge, named `sfee-charge:<charge id>`. It is acquired with the same single-statement compare-and-set as the sweep lease: UPDATE when expired, otherwise INSERT on the primary key, where a concurrent INSERT gets P2002 and the lock counts as held. The lock has a 120 s TTL, so a crashed holder blocks the charge for at most 2 minutes. The holder deletes the row when it finishes. The lock is re-entrant within one call chain (AsyncLocalStorage). No DB transaction or advisory lock is held across Stripe HTTP (the P1-3 anti-pattern, and it would be unsafe behind the pooler).
- **What runs under it:** `settleCharge`, `applyAdjustments`, and in the refund handler the critical section "is this refund id applied yet → apply → mark it applied" (`ChargeRefund.ledger_reversed`). The legacy path runs under it too.
- **Cumulative state, not increments.** Under the lock, the refunded amount is `max(row, event, Σ succeeded ChargeRefund rows of the charge)`. There is one row per Stripe refund id, and it is unique. Every payee moves from a position re-read under the lock to the target. A dispute is re-read from Stripe (`retrieveDispute`) under the lock, so an older event processed late cannot undo a newer outcome.
- **Drain before release.** The holder re-reads the refunds before it releases and applies any that landed in the meantime. A waiter that gives up after 3 s (`SFEE_CHARGE_LOCK_BUSY`, which stays inside the webhook's 5 s interactive transaction) therefore loses nothing: Stripe redelivers its webhook, which marks the refund applied without moving money. An admin refund that hits a busy lock returns the recorded refund, and the webhook applies it.
- **Ledger is absolute.** A settlement leg's slice now records `reversed_cents = slice - Σ(leg transfers net of reversals + netted)` (`SplitLedgerService.setLegPosition`), recomputed every time. A duplicate delivery can no longer add a reversal twice: the probe showed 3920 recorded against 1960 moved. Legacy head-coach transfers mirror the transfer row's total (`setReversedTotal`), and their reversal key carries the Stripe refund id. A refund that arrives before settlement is recorded as pre-reversed on the slice, so the reported net equals the target.
- An admin refund and its own webhook can both try to insert the same refund id. The loser now updates the winner's row instead of failing with P2002.

## Reconciliation

Settlement-backed purchases reconcile per charge (`settlementIdentityDrift`): Stripe gross / fee / refunded match the settlement; the four slices sum to gross; each payee's position equals their target; platform cash kept + recoveries owed - recoveries netted in = target platform fee (>= 0). Legacy purchases keep the old identity.

## Worked examples (US card 2.9% + 30c unless noted)

## Worked $100 example (round 3; owner rule: client pays $100, coach = price - actual processing - TGP 2%)

Computed with `computeChargeSplit` / `computeAdjustedTargets`. TGP's target is never below 0.

| Case | Client pays / gets back | Stripe keeps | TGP | Coach position | Money moved |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| US card (2.9% + 30c) | pays 100.00 | 3.20 | 2.00 | **94.80** | transfer 94.80 |
| International card (4.4% + 30c; +1% if Stripe converts currency, also borne by the coach) | pays 100.00 | 4.70 | 2.00 | **93.30** | transfer 93.30 |
| Partial refund $40 on the US charge (OR-111-1) | gets 40.00 back | 3.20 (not returned) | 2.00 | 60.00 - 3.20 - 2.00 = **54.80** | reversal 40.00, nothing held |
| ... the same $40 refund delivered twice, or concurrently with a second $10 refund | gets 40.00 (+10.00) back | 3.20 | 2.00 | 54.80 (44.80) | one reversal of 40.00 (reversals total 50.00), never more than 94.80 |
| Dispute lost on the US charge ($15 fee) | gets 100.00 back | 3.20 + 15.00 | 2.00 | **-20.20** | 94.80 reversed; 20.20 held from the coach's next sale(s) |
| Dispute won (Stripe keeps the $15 fee) | pays 100.00 | 3.20 + 15.00 | 2.00 | **79.80** | recovery released; 79.80 reinstated |
| Dispute won, Stripe returns the fee | pays 100.00 | 3.20 | 2.00 | 94.80 | 94.80 reinstated |

Check, partial refund: TGP received 100.00, Stripe kept 3.20, the client got 40.00 back and the coach holds 54.80, so TGP holds 100.00 - 3.20 - 40.00 - 54.80 = 2.00, which is its target.

## OR-111-1 worked examples (round 5; `test/s-fee-r5-or-111-1.spec.ts`)

US card, $100 sale: Stripe fee 3.20, TGP 2% = 2.00, coach transfer 94.80. $49 sale: Stripe fee 1.72, TGP 0.98, coach 46.30.

| Example | Client got back | Reversed from that sale's transfer | Held from next sale(s) = TGP 2% + Stripe fees (+ share not reversed) | Next sale(s) | TGP on the refunded charge after netting |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|---:|
| **1. $100 full refund** | 100.00 | 94.80 | **5.20** = 2.00 + 3.20 | next $100 sale: 94.80 - 5.20 = **89.60** transferred | **+2.00** (cash -3.20 until the next sale) |
| **2. $100 lost dispute, $15 fee** | 100.00 (bank) | 94.80 | **20.20** = 2.00 + 3.20 + 15.00 | next $100 sale: 94.80 - 20.20 = **74.60** transferred; the `dispute_lost` notice says "$20.20 is still held" and moves no money | **+2.00** |
| **3. Refused reversal after payout ($100 full refund), then a $49 sale and a $100 sale** | 100.00 | 0 (Stripe refused) | **100.00** = 2.00 + 3.20 + 94.80 not reversed | $49 sale: 46.30 netted, **0.00** transferred (status `netted`), 53.70 still held; $100 sale: 53.70 netted, **41.10** transferred, 0 held. No other sale's transfer is reversed. | **+2.00** ($49 charge +0.98, second $100 charge +2.00) |

Notice text for example 1: "A client got $100.00 back. We took $94.80 back from that sale's payout. We will hold $5.20 from your next sale." Example 2 (chargeback): "A client's bank took back $100.00 in a dispute. We took $94.80 back from that sale's payout. We will hold $20.20 from your next sale." Example 3: "A client got $100.00 back. We will hold $100.00 from your next sale." A won dispute ($15 fee kept): "You won the dispute on a $100.00 charge. We paid $79.80 back to you and released the $20.20 hold. Nothing is held from your next sale."

## Operator actions / open risks

1. **B-627-3 residual: decided by the owner (OR-111-1), no activation hold.** What a coach owes after a refund or chargeback is held from their next sale(s) by forward netting only. No payout delay, no `debit_negative_balances`, no Account Debits, no reversal of other sales. A coach who was paid out and never sells again leaves an open receivable; `SFEE_RECOVERY_OPEN alert=true payee=<id> currency=<c> open_cents=<n> ...` fires for it after 24 h (accepted residual; production has 0 paid sales). TGP's cash on the refunded charge is negative only until netting completes; the identity reports `platform_cash_cents` and `receivable_open_cents` separately.
2. **Sweeper schedule (closed in round 2).** `SettlementSweepCron` runs it every 15 minutes, see below.
3. **Head coach without a connected account (owner: keep):** the sub-coach keeps the 5% (TGP never keeps more than 2%). Recommended default: keep.
4. **ACH/bank debit (owner: keep strict):** follows the owner ruling strictly (actual fee + 2%); the old payouts-v2 50% rail-savings share stays only in the feature-flagged payouts-v2 `compute()`. Recommended default: keep strict.
5. **Guest one-time checkout** used to charge an estimated fee (max(2%, 50c) + 2.9% + 30c) and skipped the head-coach split; it now settles like every other path.
6. **Legacy subscriptions** (moot: production has 0 subscriptions and 0 purchases) created before this PR keep destination charges until they are recreated; their renewals are recorded as `legacy_destination` and keep the old (TGP-pays-fee) economics. Recommended: owner decides whether to migrate active subscriptions (follow-up).
7. (Accepted by operator with the reconciliation flag.) Legacy per-purchase ledger rows are now deduplicated by find-then-create (the old unique moved to include the charge id); concurrent legacy webhooks for one purchase could duplicate a legacy row, which reconciliation flags as drift.
8. Stripe Dashboard: confirm the platform account has `transfers` capability on every coach account (already required for the head-coach split) and that `on_behalf_of` is allowed for these accounts (already used today).
9. **Charge lock (rounds 3-4, no decision needed):** while one worker moves money on a charge, a webhook for the same charge waits up to 3 s and then fails with `SFEE_CHARGE_LOCK_BUSY`. Stripe redelivers it, and the holder has already applied the latest state, so the cost is a retried delivery and no money is lost. Round 4 fences every money step with a compare-and-set on the lease holder. A holder whose lease was taken over, or that has held the lock past its 60 s budget (half the 120 s TTL), gets `SFEE_CHARGE_LOCK_LOST` before any further write or Stripe call. A reversal it already sent is finished by the new holder under the same idempotency key, so the money moves once.
10. **Dispute fee on a won dispute:** the code follows the dispute's balance transactions. If Stripe returns the $15 fee, the coach goes back to the full net; if Stripe keeps it, the coach bears it, per the owner rule.
